fixed.w: Singular matrices have no inverse.

The rank of the 3×3 identity matrix is:
fixed.w: Rank = number of linearly independent rows. AX = B is consistent iff rank(A) = rank([A|B]); unique solution iff that rank = number of unknowns.

fixed.q: If A is orthogonal, then:
fixed.w: Symmetric: A = Aᵀ. Idempotent: A² = A. Skew-symmetric: Aᵀ = −A (diagonal zero).

fixed.q: The eigenvalues of [[2, 1], [1, 2]] are:
fixed.w: λ² − 4λ + 3 = 0. Check: sum 4 = trace, product 3 = det.

fixed.q: lim (x→0) sin x / x equals:
fixed.w: lim (1 + 1/n)ⁿ = e. lim (eˣ − 1)/x = 1.

fixed.q: d/dx (x²·eˣ) is:
fixed.w: Product rule.

fixed.q: ∫₀¹ x² dx equals:
f(x) = x³ − 3x has a local maximum at:
Rolle's theorem requires f(a) = f(b) and f continuous on [a, b] and differentiable on (a, b). It guarantees:
o: Some c in (a, b) with f'(c) = 0
fixed.w: Mean value theorem: f'(c) = (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a).

fixed.q: Two fair dice are thrown. Probability that the sum is 7?
fixed.w: 6 favourable outcomes of 36.

fixed.q: A fair coin is tossed 3 times. Probability of at least one head?
If A and B are independent, P(A ∩ B) =
fixed.w: Mutually exclusive: P(A ∩ B) = 0 and P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B).

fixed.q: For a binomial distribution B(n, p), the mean and variance are:
fixed.w: Poisson: mean = variance = λ. Uniform(a, b): mean (a + b)/2, variance (b − a)²/12.

fixed.q: The mean of 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 is ___ and the median of 3, 1, 7, 5 is ___.
fixed.w: Sorted 1, 3, 5, 7 → median (3 + 5)/2 = 4. Mode = most frequent value.

fixed.q: For a normal distribution, mean, median and mode are:
fixed.w: About 68% of values lie within ±1σ, 95% within ±2σ, 99.7% within ±3σ.

fixed.q: Newton–Raphson iteration for f(x) = 0 is:
fixed.w: Converges quadratically. Bisection halves the interval (linear, always converges for a sign change).

fixed.q: Simpson's 1/3 rule requires the number of intervals to be:
fixed.w: Simpson's 3/8 needs a multiple of 3. Trapezoidal rule: any number.

fixed.q: The number of subsets of a set with n elements is:
fixed.w: Proper subsets: 2ⁿ − 1. Relations on a set of n elements: 2^(n²).

fixed.q: A relation that is reflexive, symmetric and transitive is a(n):
fixed.w: Partial order: reflexive, antisymmetric, transitive.

fixed.q: The number of ways to arrange 5 distinct books on a shelf is:
A complete graph K₅ has how many edges?
fixed.w: n(n − 1)/2. A tree with n vertices has n − 1 edges.

fixed.q: p → q is logically equivalent to:
fixed.w: Contrapositive ¬q → ¬p is equivalent; converse q → p is not.

fixed.q: An Euler circuit exists in a connected graph iff:
o: Exactly two vertices have odd degree
fixed.w: Exactly two odd-degree vertices → Euler path (not circuit).

fixed.q: The series Σ 1/∛(n²) is:
fixed.w: Σ 1/n^(2/3) is a p-series with p = 2/3 ≤ 1, so it diverges. The official key says 'convergent', which is mathematically wrong. (The official key was wrong here; this is the corrected answer.)

fixed.q: Which method creates interpolants that are softer?
fixed.w: Piecewise-constant interpolation. Note that spline interpolation is usually what gives the smoothest interpolants.

fixed.q: The ______ interpolation method is used in probability theory and statistics, and the Gaussian process is one example.
fixed.w: Nonlinear interpolation. Gaussian-process regression (kriging) is a non-linear interpolation method.

fixed.q: Find a unit vector normal to the surface x³ + y³ + 3xyz = 3 at the point (1, 2, −1).
fixed.w: ∇f = (3x² + 3yz, 3y² + 3xz, 3xy) = (3 − 6, 12 − 3, 6) = (−3, 9, 6) ∝ (−1, 3, 2), whose length is √14. So the unit normal is (−î + 3ĵ + 2k̂)/√14.

fixed.q: Which of the following is NOT a method of solving quadratic equations?
fixed.w: Quadratics are solved by factorisation, completing the square or the quadratic formula; 'convergence' is not a method.

fixed.q: Suppose we are given values of y = f(x) for a set of values of x. The process of finding the value of y corresponding to any value x = xᵢ between x₀ and xₙ is called
fixed.w: Estimating y for an x inside the known range is interpolation; outside the range it is extrapolation.

fixed.q: Which of the following methods is used for the function y = f(x), with the given discrete set of points (xᵢ, yᵢ), i = 0, 1, 2, …, n, where the xᵢ's are NOT equispaced?
fixed.w: For unequally spaced x values, use Newton's divided-difference formula (or Lagrange).

fixed.q: AB is a tangent to a circle at B. O is the centre of the circle. If the circle radius is 40 mm and AB = 150 mm, calculate the length of AO.
fixed.w: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius, so AO = √(150² + 40²) = √24100 ≈ 155.2 mm.

fixed.q: What is the amount of rotation between two straight lines?
fixed.w: The amount of rotation between two straight lines is the angle between them.

fixed.q: A cube is a square prism. If all the sides of a cube are x, then volume = ______ and surface area = ______.
fixed.w: Cube of side x: volume x³, surface area 6x².

fixed.q: The volume of the tetrahedron bounded by the surfaces x = 0, y = 0, z = 0 and x/a + y/b + z/c = 1 is:
fixed.w: The tetrahedron cut off by x/a + y/b + z/c = 1 has volume abc/6.

fixed.q: What is the value of Δⁿ e^(ax+b)? (interval of differencing h)
fixed.w: Δe^(ax+b) = e^(a(x+h)+b) − e^(ax+b) = (e^(ah) − 1)e^(ax+b), so Δⁿ gives (e^(ah) − 1)ⁿ e^(ax+b).

fixed.q: The values of x are 1, 3, 4 and those of f(x) are 1, 27, 64. What is the polynomial equation by using the Lagrange interpolation formula?
The general solution of dy/dx = e^(x+y) is:
fixed.w: E^(−y) dy = e^x dx gives −e^(−y) = e^x + k, i.e. e^x + e^(−y) = c.

fixed.q: If u = tan⁻¹(y/x), then x ∂u/∂x + y ∂u/∂y = ?
fixed.w: U = tan⁻¹(y/x) is homogeneous of degree 0, so by Euler's theorem x uₓ + y u_y = 0.

fixed.q: If μ is an averaging operator and δⁿ is the nth central difference operator, then what is the value of μ²?
fixed.w: Μ = ½(E^½ + E^−½) and δ = E^½ − E^−½, so μ² = ¼(δ² + 4).

fixed.q: What is the number of terms in the given expression? (x² + 2/x)¹¹
fixed.w: (a + b)ⁿ has n + 1 terms, so the 11th power gives 12 terms.

fixed.q: A/An ______ is a rectangular array of numbers arranged in rows and columns enclosed by brackets.
fixed.w: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers in rows and columns.

fixed.q: Find the rank of the given matrix: [1 5 6; 2 3 4; −1 2 2]
fixed.w: Det = 1(6 − 8) − 5(4 + 4) + 6(4 + 3) = 0, and a 2×2 minor is non-zero, so the rank is 2.

fixed.q: ______ is a method of constructing new data points within the range of a discrete set of known data points.
fixed.w: Interpolation constructs new points within the range of known points.

fixed.q: Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements? i) Interpolation is a statistical method by which related known values are used to estimate an unknown value or set of values. ii) In the Inverse Distance Weighted (IDW) interpolation method, estimation of cell values is done by averaging values of sample data points in the neighbourhood of each processing cell.
fixed.w: Both interpolation statements are true.

fixed.q: If x + iy = tan(A + iB), then what is the value of x² + y² + 2x cot 2A − 2?
fixed.w: For x + iy = tan(A + iB), x² + y² + 2x cot 2A = 1, so the expression is 1 − 2 = −1.

fixed.q: What is the minimum value of the function y = x² in the interval [1, 6]?
fixed.w: Y = x² is increasing on [1, 6], so its minimum is at x = 1: y = 1.

fixed.q: If f(1) = 4 and f(5) = 6, then what is the value of f(3) using Lagrange's interpolation?
fixed.w: Linear interpolation through (1, 4) and (5, 6): f(3) = 4 + (6 − 4)(3 − 1)/4 = 5.

fixed.q: What is the maximum value of the function f(x) = 2x² − 2x + 6 in the interval [0, 2]?
fixed.w: The parabola's minimum is at x = 0.5. Compare endpoints: f(0) = 6 and f(2) = 10, so the maximum is 10.

fixed.q: The value of the integral I = ∫ from 0 to π/2 of x² sin x dx is
fixed.w: By parts: [−x² cos x + 2x sin x + 2 cos x] from 0 to π/2 = π − 2.

fixed.q: The convergence of the bisection method is
fixed.w: Bisection halves the error each step, so convergence is linear (order 1).

Which of the following comes under applied mathematics?
fixed.w: Operations research is a branch of applied mathematics.

fixed.q: Which probability calculus of views obeys particular rules?
fixed.w: Bayesian probability, which treats probability as a degree of belief obeying the calculus rules.

fixed.q: Who invented the probability definition?
fixed.w: Laplace gave the classical definition of probability.

fixed.q: Identify the generic probability density function that corresponds with discrete random variables.
fixed.w: The Poisson distribution, a discrete distribution (strictly a probability mass function).

fixed.q: Consider the following data set: 6, 20, 25, 63, 92, 101. What is the range of the data set?
fixed.w: Range = maximum − minimum = 101 − 6 = 95.

fixed.q: Which of the following is a type of Discrete Probability Distribution?
fixed.w: Poisson is discrete; log-normal, exponential and normal are continuous.

fixed.q: Which of the following helps to make predictions from data?
fixed.w: Inferential statistics draws conclusions and predictions about a population from sample data.

fixed.q: The algebraic sum of deviations is zero when measured from the ______.
fixed.w: Σ(x − x̄) = 0 only about the arithmetic mean.

fixed.q: If two dice are thrown, find the probability that the sum is neither 5 nor 9.
fixed.w: P(sum 5) = 4/36 and P(sum 9) = 4/36, so P(neither) = 28/36 = 7/9.

fixed.q: Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements? i) In probability theory, an outcome is the result of a random experiment. ii) The purpose of statistical inference is to estimate the uncertainty or sample-to-sample variation. iii) A sampling error is the difference between the true population values (called parameters) and the measured sample values (called statistics).
fixed.w: All three statements are true definitions.

fixed.q: Let P be the median of the data: 34, 28, 20, 32, 15, 9, 23, 26, 35, 16, 33, 43. If 16 and 23 are replaced by 30 and 32 respectively in the data, then let Q be the median of the resulting data. What is the value of (3P – 2Q)?
fixed.w: Sorted: …26, 28… gives P = 27. After the replacement: …30, 32… gives Q = 31. 3P − 2Q = 81 − 62 = 19.

fixed.q: What is the mean of the mode and median of the data given below? 8, 7, 5, 4, 9, 1, 3, 7, 6, 5, 2, 1, 6, 3, 9, 8, 4, 6
fixed.w: The mode is 6 (three times). The 18 sorted values have 9th and 10th values 5 and 6, so the median is 5.5. Mean of the two = (6 + 5.5)/2 = 5.75.

fixed.q: An anti-aircraft gun can take a maximum of 4 shots at an enemy plane moving away from it. The probabilities of hitting the plane at the first, second, third and fourth shot are 0.6, 0.5, 0.4 and 0.2 respectively. What is the probability that the gun hits the plane?

A ball is drawn again from the bag at random. The probability that the first ball drawn is blue, given that the second ball drawn is blue, is:
In a path graph having 'n' vertices, where n > 2, ______ is the number of vertices with degree 2.
fixed.w: In a path P_n the two end vertices have degree 1 and the remaining n − 2 have degree 2.

fixed.q: The vertex in a graph with degree one is known as ______.
fixed.w: A vertex of degree one is a pendant vertex.

fixed.q: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding about the undirected graph? I. Number of odd degree vertices is even. II. Sum of degrees of all vertices is even.
fixed.w: By the handshaking lemma, the sum of degrees = 2|E| is even, so the number of odd-degree vertices is even. Both are true.

fixed.q: The number of edges in a regular graph of degree 'd' with 'n' vertices is
fixed.w: The sum of degrees is n·d = 2|E|, so |E| = nd/2.

fixed.q: The solution of the recurrence relation a_r = a_(r−1) + 2a_(r−2) with a0 = 2, a1 = 7 is
fixed.w: The characteristic roots are 2 and −1, so a_r = c1·2^r + c2(−1)^r. From a0 = 2 and a1 = 7, c1 = 3 and c2 = −1.

fixed.q: The maximum degree of any vertex in a simple graph with n vertices is
fixed.w: In a simple graph a vertex can be adjacent to at most the other n − 1 vertices.
Option C. Note: A − B = {1, 3} and B − C = {4}, so the Cartesian product is really {(1, 4), (3, 4)}. The key treats the answer as {1, 3, 4}.

fixed.q: A can is filled with 5 paise coins. Another can is filled with 10 paise coins. Another can is filled with 25 paise coins. All the cans are given wrong labels. If the can labelled 25 paise does not have the 10 paise coins, what will the can labelled 10 paise have?
fixed.w: The can labelled 25 holds neither 25 (wrong label) nor 10 (given), so it holds 5. The can labelled 10 can't hold 10, so it holds 25.

fixed.q: The sum of the eigenvalues of a square matrix equals its:
fixed.w: Sum of eigenvalues = trace (sum of the diagonal). Product of eigenvalues = determinant.

fixed.q: A system AX = B has a unique solution when:
fixed.w: Equal ranks equal to n give a unique solution. Equal ranks less than n give infinitely many. Unequal ranks give no solution.

fixed.q: A square matrix A with Aᵀ = −A is called:
fixed.w: Skew-symmetric: Aᵀ = −A, so its diagonal elements are all zero. Symmetric: Aᵀ = A. Orthogonal: AAᵀ = I.

fixed.q: The derivative of eˣ with respect to x is:
fixed.w: eˣ is its own derivative. d/dx(ln x) = 1/x.

fixed.q: At a point of local maximum of f(x):
fixed.w: At a stationary point, f″ < 0 gives a maximum and f″ > 0 gives a minimum.

fixed.q: ∫₀¹ x dx equals:
fixed.w: ∫x dx = x²/2, evaluated from 0 to 1 gives 1/2.

fixed.q: For a Poisson distribution with parameter λ:
fixed.w: A special property of the Poisson distribution: mean and variance are both λ.

fixed.q: The empirical relation between mean, median and mode for a moderately skewed distribution is:
fixed.w: Karl Pearson's relation: Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean.

fixed.q: The value of the correlation coefficient r always lies between:
fixed.w: r = +1: perfect positive, −1: perfect negative, 0: no linear correlation.

fixed.q: The variance of a data set is 16. Its standard deviation is:
fixed.w: SD = √variance = √16 = 4.

fixed.q: The order of convergence of the Newton–Raphson method is:
fixed.w: Newton–Raphson converges quadratically. Bisection is linear. The secant method is about 1.618.

fixed.q: A tree with n vertices has how many edges?
fixed.w: A tree is connected and acyclic, so it always has n − 1 edges.

fixed.q: By the handshaking lemma, the sum of the degrees of all vertices equals:
fixed.w: Each edge adds 2 to the total degree, so the number of odd-degree vertices is always even.

fixed.q: The inverse of a 2×2 matrix [[a, b], [c, d]] is:
fixed.w: Swap the diagonal entries, negate the off-diagonal entries and divide by the determinant ad − bc.

fixed.q: The rank of a non-zero matrix in which all rows are multiples of the first row is:
o: Equal to the number of rows
fixed.w: Only one linearly independent row, so the rank is 1.

fixed.q: If λ is an eigenvalue of an invertible matrix A, then an eigenvalue of A⁻¹ is:
fixed.w: From Ax = λx, A⁻¹x = (1/λ)x. Similarly Aᵏ has eigenvalue λᵏ.

fixed.q: The determinant of a matrix with two identical rows is:
fixed.w: Two equal rows make the rows linearly dependent, so the determinant is 0.

fixed.q: The derivative of sin x is:
fixed.w: d/dx sin x = cos x; d/dx cos x = −sin x.

fixed.q: lim (x→∞) (1 + 1/x)ˣ equals:
fixed.w: This is the standard limit that defines e ≈ 2.718.

fixed.q: Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem states that there is a c in (a, b) with:
fixed.w: LMVT: the tangent at some c is parallel to the chord. Rolle's theorem is the special case f(a) = f(b), giving f′(c) = 0.

fixed.q: Bayes' theorem is used to find:
o: The probability of a cause given an observed effect (posterior)
fixed.w: P(A|B) = P(B|A)P(A)/P(B): it updates prior probabilities with evidence.

fixed.q: A card is drawn from a standard deck of 52. The probability that it is a king or a heart is:
For a normal distribution, the total area under the curve is:
fixed.w: Any probability density function has total area 1; the normal curve is symmetric about its mean.

fixed.q: The median of 7, 3, 9, 1, 5 is:
fixed.w: Sorted: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9; the middle value is 5.

fixed.q: The bisection method requires f(a) and f(b) to:
fixed.w: A sign change on [a, b] guarantees a root (for continuous f); the interval is halved each step.

fixed.q: The trapezoidal rule integrates exactly polynomials of degree up to:
fixed.w: The trapezoidal rule is exact for straight lines. Simpson's 1/3 rule is exact up to degree 3.

fixed.q: The number of ways to choose 3 objects from 7 distinct objects is:
fixed.w: C(7, 3) = 7!/(3!·4!) = 35. Ordered arrangements would be P(7, 3) = 210.

fixed.q: If 10 pigeons are put into 9 holes, at least one hole has at least 2 pigeons. This is the:
fixed.w: The pigeonhole principle: n + 1 objects into n boxes forces a box with at least 2.

fixed.q: The order of the differential equation d²y/dx² + 3(dy/dx)³ + y = 0 is:
fixed.w: Order = highest derivative present (d²y/dx² → 2). Degree = power of that highest derivative (here 1).

fixed.q: The degree of the differential equation (d²y/dx²)³ + (dy/dx)⁴ + y = 0 is:
fixed.w: Degree is the power of the highest-order derivative (d²y/dx²), which is 3.

fixed.q: The general solution of dy/dx = ky is:
fixed.w: Separate variables: dy/y = k dx → ln y = kx + c → y = Ceᵏˣ.

fixed.q: The integrating factor of dy/dx + Py = Q (P, Q functions of x) is:
fixed.w: Multiplying by I.F. = e^(∫P dx) makes the left side d/dx(y·I.F.).

fixed.q: The general solution of y″ − 5y′ + 6y = 0 is:
fixed.w: Auxiliary equation m² − 5m + 6 = 0 gives m = 2, 3 (real, distinct).

fixed.q: If the auxiliary equation has a repeated root m, the complementary function is:
fixed.w: A repeated root needs the extra factor x for the second independent solution.

fixed.q: M dx + N dy = 0 is an exact differential equation if:
fixed.w: The exactness test is ∂M/∂y = ∂N/∂x.

fixed.q: The Laplace transform of 1 is:
The Laplace transform of eᵃᵗ is:
fixed.w: L{eᵃᵗ} = 1/(s − a) for s > a.

fixed.q: The Laplace transform of sin at is:
fixed.w: L{sin at} = a/(s² + a²); L{cos at} = s/(s² + a²).

fixed.q: The Laplace transform of tⁿ is:
fixed.w: L{tⁿ} = n!/sⁿ⁺¹; for example L{t} = 1/s².

fixed.q: The Fourier series of an even function on (−π, π) contains:
o: Both sine and cosine terms always
fixed.w: For even f, bₙ = 0, so only a₀ and cosine terms remain. An odd function gives only sine terms.

fixed.q: The curl of the gradient of any scalar field is:
fixed.w: curl(grad φ) = 0, and div(curl F) = 0 as well.

fixed.q: A vector field F with div F = 0 is called:
fixed.w: Solenoidal: ∇·F = 0. Irrotational: ∇×F = 0.

fixed.q: If r = xi + yj + zk, then div r equals:
The Cauchy–Riemann equations for f = u + iv to be analytic are:
fixed.w: Analytic functions satisfy uₓ = v_y and u_y = −vₓ (with continuous partial derivatives).

fixed.q: The modulus of the complex number 3 + 4i is:
Rejecting the null hypothesis when it is actually true is a:
fixed.w: Type I: reject a true H₀ (probability α, the level of significance). Type II: accept a false H₀ (probability β).

fixed.q: The t-test is mainly used when:
o: The sample is small (n < 30) and σ is unknown
The sample is very large and σ is known
fixed.w: The t-test is for small samples. For large samples the z-test is used. χ² is for counts/goodness of fit.

fixed.q: The degrees of freedom for a χ² test on a contingency table with r rows and c columns are:
fixed.w: For an r × c table, d.f. = (r − 1)(c − 1).

fixed.q: The standard error of the sample mean is:
fixed.w: SE of the mean = σ/√n; it falls as the sample size grows.

fixed.q: The z-value used for a 95% two-sided confidence interval is about:
Newton's forward difference formula is best for interpolating near:
fixed.w: Forward differences are used near the start; backward differences near the end; Stirling/Bessel (central) near the middle.

fixed.q: For unequally spaced data, a suitable interpolation formula is:
fixed.w: Lagrange and Newton's divided-difference formulas work for unequal intervals; forward/backward/central need equal spacing.

fixed.q: The relation between the forward difference operator Δ and the shift operator E is:
fixed.w: Δ = E − 1, while the backward operator ∇ = 1 − E⁻¹.

fixed.q: For a polynomial of degree n with equally spaced x, the nth forward differences are:
fixed.w: nth differences of a degree-n polynomial are constant, and (n+1)th differences are zero.

fixed.q: d/dx (sin x) is:
fixed.w: d/dx cos x = −sin x; d/dx tan x = sec²x.

fixed.q: ∫ eˣ dx is:
fixed.w: ∫ 1/x dx = ln|x| + C.

fixed.q: f(x) = x² − 4x + 3 has a minimum at x =
fixed.w: f'(x) = 2x − 4 = 0 gives x = 2, and f'' = 2 > 0, so it is a minimum.

fixed.q: The Newton–Raphson iteration formula is:
fixed.w: It converges quadratically near a simple root.

fixed.q: The bisection method needs a starting interval [a, b] such that:
o: f(a) and f(b) have opposite signs
a and b are both roots
fixed.w: It halves the interval each step and converges linearly.

fixed.q: The trapezoidal rule approximates the area under a curve using:
fixed.w: Simpson's 1/3 rule fits parabolas and needs an even number of intervals.

fixed.q: Two fair coins are tossed. The probability of getting at least one head is:
fixed.w: 1 − P(no heads) = 1 − 1/4.

fixed.q: A fair die is rolled. The probability of getting a number greater than 4 is:
fixed.w: The outcomes 5 and 6 give 2/6.

fixed.q: The mean of a binomial distribution with n trials and success probability p is:
fixed.w: The variance is npq, where q = 1 − p.

fixed.q: The mode of 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 4, 9 is:
fixed.w: The most frequent value.

fixed.q: For a moderately skewed distribution, the empirical relation is:
fixed.w: Karl Pearson's relation.

fixed.q: Standard deviation is the square root of the:
fixed.w: The coefficient of variation is SD/mean × 100.

theory.Matrices:
• Eigenvalues of triangular/diagonal matrices = diagonal entries; Σλ = trace, Πλ = det. |kA| = kⁿ|A|. Singular ⇔ det 0. Orthogonal AAᵀ = I.
• Rank = independent rows; AX = B consistent iff rank A = rank [A|B]; unique iff = number of unknowns.
theory.Calculus:
• lim sin x/x = 1; (1 + 1/n)ⁿ → e. Product rule (uv)' = u'v + uv'. Maxima: f' = 0, f'' < 0.
• Rolle: f(a) = f(b) ⇒ f'(c) = 0. MVT: f'(c) = (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a). ∫xⁿ = xⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1).
theory.Probability:
• Independent: P(A∩B) = P(A)P(B). Mutually exclusive: P(A∩B) = 0. At least one = 1 − P(none).
• Binomial mean np, variance npq; Poisson mean = variance = λ; uniform mean (a+b)/2, variance (b−a)²/12.
theory.Statistics: • Median of even count = average of middle two. Normal: mean = median = mode; 68-95-99.7 rule.
theory.Numerical methods: • Newton–Raphson xₙ₊₁ = xₙ − f/f' (quadratic). Bisection (linear, always converges with a sign change). Simpson 1/3: even intervals; 3/8: multiples of 3; trapezoidal: any.
theory.Discrete maths:
• Subsets 2ⁿ; relations 2^(n²). Equivalence: reflexive, symmetric, transitive. Partial order: reflexive, antisymmetric, transitive.
• n! arrangements; nCr, nPr. Kₙ has n(n − 1)/2 edges. Euler circuit: all degrees even; Euler path: exactly 0 or 2 odd vertices.
• p → q ≡ ¬p ∨ q ≡ ¬q → ¬p (contrapositive).
theory.Differential equations:
• Order = highest derivative; degree = power of that derivative (after clearing radicals/fractions).
• Variables separable; dy/dx = ky → y = Ceᵏˣ.
• Linear: dy/dx + Py = Q, I.F. = e^(∫P dx), solution y·I.F. = ∫Q·I.F. dx + C.
• Exact: M dx + N dy = 0 with ∂M/∂y = ∂N/∂x.
• Constant coefficients: auxiliary equation roots m₁ ≠ m₂ → C₁e^(m₁x) + C₂e^(m₂x); repeated m → (C₁ + C₂x)eᵐˣ; complex α ± iβ → e^(αx)(C₁cos βx + C₂sin βx).
theory.Transforms & series:
• Laplace: L{1} = 1/s, L{tⁿ} = n!/sⁿ⁺¹, L{eᵃᵗ} = 1/(s − a), L{sin at} = a/(s² + a²), L{cos at} = s/(s² + a²). Linear; first shifting: L{eᵃᵗf(t)} = F(s − a).
• Fourier series on (−π, π): f = a₀/2 + Σ(aₙ cos nx + bₙ sin nx). Even f → only cosines (bₙ = 0); odd f → only sines (a₀ = aₙ = 0).
theory.Vector & complex analysis:
• grad φ (vector, normal to the surface φ = c), div F (scalar), curl F (vector).
• curl grad φ = 0; div curl F = 0. div r = 3, curl r = 0.
• Solenoidal: div F = 0. Irrotational: curl F = 0 (then F = grad φ).
• Complex: |a + ib| = √(a² + b²); Euler e^(iθ) = cos θ + i sin θ. Analytic f = u + iv ⇔ Cauchy–Riemann uₓ = v_y, u_y = −vₓ.
theory.Statistical inference:
• H₀ (null) vs H₁ (alternative). Type I error: reject true H₀ (α = level of significance). Type II: accept false H₀ (β). Power = 1 − β.
• z-test: large samples (n ≥ 30) or σ known; t-test: small samples, σ unknown (d.f. n − 1); χ²: goodness of fit / independence (d.f. (r − 1)(c − 1)); F-test: ratio of variances (ANOVA).
• SE of mean = σ/√n. CI z-values: 90% 1.645, 95% 1.96, 99% 2.58.
theory.Interpolation:
• Operators: Δ = E − 1 (forward), ∇ = 1 − E⁻¹ (backward), E f(x) = f(x + h).
• nth differences of a degree-n polynomial are constant.
• Equal intervals: Newton forward (near start), Newton backward (near end), Gauss/Stirling/Bessel (central, middle of table).
• Unequal intervals: Lagrange, Newton's divided differences.
• Extrapolation = estimating outside the table range.
